candidate.answerReason: The displays repeat in the cycle 5, -1/4, 4/5, 5. Since 100 = 3 × 33 + 1, the final display is -1/4 = -0.25.

methods.label: Find a repeating cycle
methods.explanation:
Track the displays until the starting value returns. The first three presses give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{1-5}&=-\frac14,\\
\frac{1}{1-(-\frac14)}&=\frac45,\\
\frac{1}{1-\frac45}&=5.
\end{aligned}
\]
All three denominators are nonzero. Once \(5\) returns, the same rule produces the same three displays again, so every three presses return the calculator to \(5\). None of the displays in this cycle is \(1\), so every later press is also defined.

Since \(100=3\cdot33+1\), the first 99 presses complete 33 cycles. The final press changes \(5\) to \(-\frac14=-0.25\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: Verifies a three-press cycle by direct fraction arithmetic, then counts complete cycles and one remaining press.
